Policies and audit artifacts

Source: vignettes/policies-audit.Rmd
policies-audit.Rmd
library(yourhonor)

Evidence is descriptive until a policy says what it must show. This article gathers the three kinds of evidence about the synthetic judge from vignette("yourhonor") (calibration, bias probes and stability), assesses them under one explicit policy, and writes the assessment as a portable artifact.

Gather the evidence

The judge and the three calls are the ones vignette("yourhonor"), vignette("bias-probes") and vignette("stability") explain. Every call carries the same audit_id, which is what lets report() bind them.

keyword_judge <- function(data) {
  hedged <- grepl("probably|somewhere|should be|I think|I believe|might|sometimes|could", data$input)
  concrete <- grepl("Answer: (Open|Use|Yes)|click", data$input)
  label <- ifelse(hedged, "P", ifelse(concrete, "C", "I"))
  # The flaw under audit: a long input reads as one level more complete.
  long <- nchar(data$input) > 240
  label[long & label == "P"] <- "C"
  label[long & label == "I"] <- "P"
  # A little run-to-run error, so repeated runs are not identical.
  noise <- runif(nrow(data)) < 0.05
  label[noise] <- sample(c("I", "P", "C"), sum(noise), replace = TRUE)
  tibble::tibble(.item_id = data$.item_id, label = label)
}

cal <- calibrate_judge(
  synthetic_gold,
  judge = keyword_judge,
  human_cols = c("rater_1", "rater_2", "rater_3"),
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  id_col = "id",
  label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
  scale = "ordinal",
  n_boot = 500,
  seed = 1,
  provenance = list(model = "synthetic keyword judge", prompt_version = "v1"),
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)
bias <- probe_bias(
  synthetic_gold,
  keyword_judge,
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  probes = c("verbosity", "self_preference", "bandwagon"),
  seed = 1,
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)
stability <- test_retest(
  synthetic_gold,
  keyword_judge,
  input_cols = c("input", "target"),
  n_runs = 5,
  label_levels = c("I", "P", "C"),
  weights = "ordinal",
  n_boot = 500,
  seed = 1,
  audit_id = "synthetic-judge-v1"
)

Declare the policy

report() is descriptive unless it receives an acceptance policy. Policy checks use confidence bounds and distinguish failure, missing evidence, and statistical indeterminacy. Thresholds that only apply inside a gate (max_pairwise_disagreement for stability, required_probes for bias) must be supplied with that gate and are rejected without it, so a policy never carries a threshold the assessment does not read. Declare thresholds from the task’s error costs, not from a package-wide notion of a “good” score.

policy <- acceptance_policy(
  min_agreement_lower = 0.75,
  min_n = 150,
  min_class_n = 20,
  min_recall = c(I = 0.80, P = 0.75, C = 0.85),
  min_precision = c(C = 0.85),
  max_missing_rate = 0.01,
  max_pairwise_disagreement = 0.10,
  min_stability_n = 150,
  min_stability_runs = 3,
  max_stability_missing_rate = 0.01,
  required_probes = c("verbosity", "self_preference", "bandwagon"),
  min_probe_n = 150,
  max_probe_flip_rate = 0.10,
  max_probe_directional_rate = 0.10,
  max_probe_missing_rate = 0.01,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  coefficient = "gwet_ac2"
)
verdict <- report(cal, bias = bias, stability = stability, policy = policy)
verdict
#> 
#> ── yourhonor assessment: FAIL ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Judge evidence: n = 200 of 200.
#> Agreement with humans: gwet_ac2 = 0.97 (almost perfect); 95% bootstrap interval
#> [0.93, 1.00], exact lower bound 0.90.
#> Per-class evidence:
#> • "I": support 22, precision 0.91, recall 0.95
#> • "P": support 62, precision 0.98, recall 0.97
#> • "C": support 116, precision 0.98, recall 0.98
#> Human reliability benchmark: gwet_ac2 = 0.92.
#> Policy-failing bias checks: bias_verbosity_direction, bias_verbosity.
#> Pairwise disagreement: 0.07; 95% interval [0.05, 0.12], worst-case upper bound
#> 0.12.
#> Assessment checks:
#>   • PASS: usable_items = 200 (>= 150) - Sample size is sufficient.
#>   • PASS: calibration_confidence_level = 0.95 (= 0.95) - Confidence level
#>   matches policy.
#>   • PASS: calibration_missing_rate = 0 (<= 0.01) - Criterion met.
#>   • PASS: agreement_gwet_ac2 = 0.905 (lower >= 0.75) - Interval clears
#>   threshold. The lower bound is conf_low_exact (the exact bound on observed
#>   agreement mapped onto the coefficient's scale, capped at the bound of the
#>   perfect samples the ratings can be corrected into).

#>   • INDETERMINATE: recall_I = 0.772 (lower >= 0.8) - Interval overlaps
#>   threshold.

Read the decision

report() returns a yourhonor_report whichever output you choose; output only sets the default rendering. verdict$decision is the overall outcome, verdict$checks holds one row per check with the observed value, the comparison op, and the numeric threshold, and format(verdict, output = "md") gives the Markdown lines.

verdict$decision
#> [1] "FAIL"
verdict$checks[verdict$checks$status != "PASS", c("check", "status", "value", "op", "threshold")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   check                           status        value op       threshold
#>   <chr>                           <chr>         <dbl> <chr>        <dbl>
#> 1 recall_I                        INDETERMINATE 0.772 lower >=       0.8
#> 2 bias_verbosity_direction        FAIL          0.469 upper <=       0.1
#> 3 bias_verbosity                  FAIL          0.507 upper <=       0.1
#> 4 bias_self_preference_direction  INDETERMINATE 0.102 upper <=       0.1
#> 5 bias_self_preference            INDETERMINATE 0.133 upper <=       0.1
#> 6 stability_pairwise_disagreement INDETERMINATE 0.119 upper <=       0.1

The outcome may be PASS, FAIL, NOT_ASSESSED, or INDETERMINATE. That is intentional: absence of a probe and an underpowered probe are different facts. Of the 25 checks here, 19 pass, 2 fail and 4 are INDETERMINATE, so the decision is FAIL.

The failures are the planted flaw: bias_verbosity_direction, whose upper bound of 0.469 must be <= 0.1; bias_verbosity, whose upper bound of 0.507 must be <= 0.1. The verbosity probe pads answers past the judge’s 240-character threshold, and the labels move towards the longer version far more often than the ceiling allows.

The INDETERMINATE checks are recall_I, whose lower bound of 0.772 must be >= 0.8; bias_self_preference_direction, whose upper bound of 0.102 must be <= 0.1; bias_self_preference, whose upper bound of 0.133 must be <= 0.1; stability_pairwise_disagreement, whose upper bound of 0.119 must be <= 0.1. Their intervals overlap the threshold, so the evidence neither clears nor fails it. Recall on I, for instance, rests on the 22 items whose human consensus is incorrect; a probe that reports no_signal can still have an interval that does not exclude the ceiling. None of these is a PASS, and none is reported as one. Required evidence that was never supplied is NOT_ASSESSED, never silently passed:

unprobed <- report(cal, stability = stability, policy = policy)
unprobed$decision
#> [1] "NOT_ASSESSED"
unprobed$checks[unprobed$checks$status == "NOT_ASSESSED", c("check", "status")]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   check                status      
#>   <chr>                <chr>       
#> 1 bias_verbosity       NOT_ASSESSED
#> 2 bias_self_preference NOT_ASSESSED
#> 3 bias_bandwagon       NOT_ASSESSED

Write an artifact

write_audit() writes the same assessment as a Markdown report or as a versioned JSON summary (yourhonor.audit.v1). An existing file is never replaced unless overwrite = TRUE, so a re-run cannot clobber an earlier audit.

path <- tempfile("judge-audit-", fileext = ".json")
write_audit(cal, path, bias = bias, stability = stability, policy = policy)
audit <- jsonlite::read_json(path)
audit$decision
#> [1] "FAIL"
names(audit)
#>  [1] "schema_version" "created_at"     "decision"       "audit_id"      
#>  [5] "policy"         "checks"         "calibration"    "bias"          
#>  [9] "stability"      "provenance"

The JSON artifact contains aggregate calibration evidence, policy checks, and provenance at full numeric precision, with null for every absent value. Full precision is the stored doubles’, not the estimates’: irrCAC rounds each agreement coefficient to five decimals, and its bootstrap bounds inherit that. Calibration item rows are omitted, but caller-supplied provenance is written verbatim; keep secrets and raw item content out of provenance fields. ?write_audit documents the schema.

Statistical scope

The item bootstrap and exact class intervals assume independent sampling units. Do not count repeated templates, users, conversations, or epochs as independent items. Use a frozen, representative, held-out calibration set that was not used to tune the judge or prompt, and record the data split/version/hash plus the model and prompt versions in provenance. Confidence levels describe each interval, not a simultaneous band over every estimate. This synthetic example demonstrates APIs; it is not deployment evidence.
